deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is one of the Gauss–Weber damping (induction) experiments with a magnetometer whose needle swings inside a multiplier coil. 'offen' means the coil circuit is open. 'geschlossen' means it is closed, so induced currents add electromagnetic damping. Each row gives the oscillation number n, the clock time of the turning point (period about 42.35 s), the swing amplitude A in scale divisions, and log10 A.

(1) First open-circuit group, n = 140–144:
- A = 380.5, 379.35, 378.0, 376.85, 375.15.
- log10 A = 2.58035, 2.57904, 2.57749, 2.57617, 2.57420. For n = 144 Gauss first wrote 2.57… and corrected it to 7420.
- The mean of the five logs, assigned to the middle oscillation n = 142, is L(142) = 12.88725/5 = 2.57745.

(2) Second open-circuit group, n = 156–160:
- A = 363.2, 361.5, 359.85, 358.9, 358.15.
- log10 A = 2.56015, 2.55811, 2.55612, 2.55497, 2.55406.
- Mean L(158) = 12.78341/5 = 2.55668.

(3) Logarithmic decrement per oscillation, in units of 10^-5 of the Briggsian log:
- D.L. = (L(142) − L(158))/16 = 0.02077/16 = 0.001298, written 129.8.
- It belongs to the mid-epoch n = 150 = (142+158)/2.
- The same procedure on the previous page gives 116.5 (open, epoch 104, from n = 96 and 112) and 657.7 (closed, epoch 127, from n = 119 and 135).
- The thermometer reads 6.8 °C.

(4) Recapitulation: open and closed series alternate. Open decrements: 110.0 (No. 10), 111.0 (57), 116.5 (104), 129.8 (150). Closed decrements: 652.9 (34), 658.4 (81), 657.7 (127). Pencil columns (my reading of what they are): at each epoch Gauss linearly interpolates the decrement of the other state from its two neighbours, then takes closed minus open. That difference is the damping caused by the induced currents alone.
- No. 34: open ≈ 110.0 + (24/47)·1.0 = 110.5; difference 652.9 − 110.5 = 542.4.
- No. 57: closed ≈ 652.9 + (23/47)·5.5 = 655.6; difference 655.6 − 111.0 = 544.6.
- No. 81: open ≈ 111.0 + (24/47)·5.5 = 113.8; 658.4 − 113.8 = 544.6, but 544.8 is written.
- No. 104: closed ≈ 658.4 − (23/46)·0.7 = 658.05, taken as 658.0; difference 658.0 − 116.5 = 541.5.
- No. 127: open ≈ 116.5 + (23/46)·13.3 = 123.15, taken as 123.1; difference 657.7 − 123.1 = 534.6.
- The arithmetic mean of the five differences is 2707.9/5 = 541.58, i.e. an induction decrement of about 0.0054158 per oscillation in log10.

The open-circuit decrement drifts upward (110 to 129.8) as the amplitude falls. This is why Gauss interpolates in time rather than using one fixed air-damping value.
errors: Recapitulation No. 81: 658.4 − 113.8 = 544.6, but the pencil value is 544.8, a slip of +0.2 (unless the interpolated open value was taken as 113.6). This raises the final mean by 0.04: the correct mean is 541.54 rather than 541.58.

The clock times for n = 141–143 as written/transcribed (18'10.9, [18']53.05, 19'5.45) are inconsistent with the 42.35 s period. The expected times from 140 (17'58.5) and 144 (20'47.85) are 18'40.85, 19'23.2 and 20'5.55. The fractional seconds fit, so this is a misreading or a minute/tens-of-seconds slip. The times are not used in the computations.
Minor rounding choices: 658.05 is rounded to 658.0 and 123.15 to 123.1. These are harmless.
All logarithms, both group means (2.57745, 2.55668) and the decrement 129.8 check out correctly.

results.what: Logarithmic decrement of magnetometer oscillations: mean of log amplitudes over two 5-swing groups 16 swings apart, difference divided by 16
results.modern_name: logarithmic decrement of a damped oscillator (estimated from grouped amplitude means)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and W. Weber, Göttingen magnetic observations, 1830s

results.what: Separating electromagnetic (induction) damping from air/residual damping: alternate open and closed circuit, interpolate the other state linearly in time, take differences and average them (result 541.58 ×10^-5)
results.modern_name: eddy-current/induction damping measurement with linear drift correction (bracketing/interpolation of a control series)
results.usually_credited_to: W. Weber (damping/'Dämpfer' experiments, c. 1837 onward), with Gauss

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine laboratory reductions from the well-documented Gauss–Weber magnetometer/induction damping experiments. Logarithmic decrement and linear interpolation of control measurements are standard and already associated with Gauss and Weber.

checkable.asserts: log10 of the first group's amplitudes
mean log of the first group
log10 of the second group's amplitudes
mean log of the second group, 2.55668
induction decrement at No. 81 ≈ 544.6 (not 544.8 as written)

transcription_corrections: Row 144: Gauss overwrote the log as 2.57420 (the '7420' is his correction above the line). The full value should read 2.57420.

The times for rows 141–143 are probably 18'40.9, 19'23.05, 20'5.45 on period grounds. Either the transcription (10.9, 53.05, minute 19) is a misreading or Gauss slipped. Unverifiable from the period alone.

In the Recapitulation, the pencil columns (110.5/542.4, 655.6/544.6, 113.8/544.8, 658.0/541.5, 123.1/534.6, mean 541.58) are interpolated values and differences added in pencil, distinct from the ink data. The header 'geschloss[en]' is abbreviated.
